thread:
Tara L: Quick sync — putting a short proposal up for per-org rate limits. Leaning toward a token-bucket (TPM) + fixed concurrency cap hybrid rather than RPM-only. Want to capture streaming token accounting and enterprise burst behavior. Thoughts?

Kevin M: Token-bucket + concurrency makes sense. Token-bucket handles long-running streaming calls better. RPM is too coarse for variable token sizes (:nod:).

Nina S: Important: embeddings vs chat have very different token profiles. We should consider separate TPM buckets per feature (embeddings TPM, chat TPM) or weight tokens. Otherwise an embedding-heavy org could starve chat traffic.

Sam R: Also think about enforcement point. Router-level should do quick rejects; edge/proxy can apply best-effort queuing while dedicated infra enforces hard caps. We need consistent failure semantics (429 + Retry-After).

Maria P: UI ask: console needs to show "effective limit" computed from plan + overrides, plus a live "burst remaining" gauge and next-refill ETA. Customers keep asking why they saw a burst then immediately got throttled.

Tara L: Agreed on console. Proposal: show per-org effective TPM and concurrency, plus a short history bar for recent throttles (count + pct). Also an endpoint to fetch current burst_remaining for dashboards.

Kevin M: One concern: how do we compute tokens for streaming partial responses? Do we debit on send or on accept? If we debit on send we can overcommit network; if on accept we risk unbounded queuing. My preference: debit when we start streaming first chunk, then per-chunk debit as sent.

Nina S: For evals/long-run streams we should have a soft pre-authorization token charge (small reserve) to avoid clients holding connections and gaming the system. If they exceed, we either drain or cap.

Sam R: FWIW, our load tests with a token-bucket + concurrency cap handled bursts better — fewer 429 spikes — but we saw more queued latency at 95th pct. Attached quick config we tested:

```yaml
policy:
  org_id: org_123
  tpm: 120000  # tokens per minute
  concurrency: 40
  burst_capacity: 80
  preauth_reserve: 5  # reserve tokens on stream start
  grace_tokens: 10    # allow short overages for enterprise
```

Maria P: Love the config. UX question: for grace_tokens (enterprise) do we surface exhaustion events as warnings in console (not just throttles)? Customers want to know when they're dipping into grace.

Tara L: Yes — surface warnings + automated notifications (email/webhook). Also add metric tag "used_grace=true" for billing/alerts.

Kevin M: Edge case: per-key vs per-org. If an org creates many keys, do we enforce per-key concurrency AND global org concurrency? I think: per-key soft throttle + per-org hard cap. That prevents one key from hogging while allowing small keys to operate.

Nina S: Agree. Per-key RPM for free-tier to limit noisy actors, per-org TPM + concurrency for global control.

Sam R: Implementation note: router needs quick path to evaluate both buckets. We'll use a two-level token check: check org bucket then key bucket. If org fails -> immediate 429. If key fails -> 429 with message hinting to rotate key or contact support.

ops-bot: Canary deploy queued for rate-limiter v2 to 5 orgs: org_123, org_456, org_789, org_qa1, org_beta. Scheduled 2026-11-02T02:00Z.

Tara L: Rollout plan:
- Beta with 5 tenants (ops-bot list) for 2 weeks.
- Collect metrics: throttle_count, throttle_pct, p95 latency while queued, number of grace usages.
- Add console panels and webhook alerts before GA.

Maria P: Also add a small "simulate" button in console so customers can run a 1-minute synthetic to see effective limits. Cheap but useful.

Kevin M: One more: define error codes for reasons: ORG_TPM_EXCEEDED, ORG_CONCURRENCY_EXCEEDED, KEY_RATE_EXCEEDED. Makes debugging easier.

Tara L: Good call. I'll update the doc with codes + UA/429 formats and a sample SDK snippet for handling Retry-After and error codes. Target: ship beta config + console widgets next sprint. :thumbsup:
